assigned.title: A Windows build that CI actually produces
assigned.acceptance: An installable Windows artifact is produced by CI on a windows-latest runner. MEASURED STARTING POINT: every job in .github/workflows/ci.yml is ubuntu-latest, no Windows runner exists, and nothing in this repository builds, packages, signs, installs or updates a Windows application. THIS IS ALSO THE ONLY WAY THIS WORK CAN BE BUILT AT ALL FROM THE ENGINEERING SESSION: the cloud container has a Linux-only Rust toolchain and the linked machine exposes a Linux VM, so no Windows binary can be produced or run here, and a windows-latest job is the substitute for a developer machine rather than a nicety. REQUIRED: the job builds the sidecar, the shell and the installer, and uploads the artifact. REQUIRED: application identity -- product name, publisher, icons, a version scheme derived from one source rather than restated in three manifests. REQUIRED: application data, log and cache locations under the correct Windows known folders, stated and tested, not scattered beside the executable. REQUIRED: the job fails on a real failure; no continue-on-error and no || true, on the rule the e2e job already states. NOT IN SCOPE: code signing, which needs an owner-held certificate and belongs in LAST_MILE.

build.evidence:
`.github/workflows/windows.yml` -> "Windows package" run #2, https://github.com/CrownOwlP/project-liberty/actions/runs/36639952960, job 109649614103, commit 65a47d5a481cb6fcbc599add010d9ffade70b43e, branch codex/pl-ai-0001-repair. STATUS SUCCESS, 8m 33s (job 8m 28s), windows-latest. Every step green, none skipped, and the workflow carries no `continue-on-error` and no `|| true`: Set up job, checkout@v4, setup-node@v4, pinned Rust toolchain (16s), rust-cache@v2, Install dependencies (35s), Build the application server for the desktop target (25s), Lay out the packaged sidecar (1s), Build the Windows installers (4m 54s), Publish the artifact inventory (1s), Install the MSI / verify it landed / uninstall it (18s), two uploads. One annotation, a GitHub deprecation notice about Node 20 actions; not a product failure.

THE INVENTORY, TRANSCRIBED FROM THE STEP LOG:
  artifact-inventory: 2 artifact(s), unsigned
   msi   2be24f70f9c58601541f9f09b3cd0ab65440a83a89f023d888e7eb5b1cb39912   45568824 B   msi/Project Liberty_0.1.0_x64_en-US.msi
   nsis  ece53242a222701d461cafebe54ba1a5122f68762f659532ecc6ea0762c00151   29716172 B   nsis/Project Liberty_0.1.0_x64-setup.exe
  artifact-inventory: written to D:\a\project-liberty\project-liberty\artifact-inventory.json
  "signed": false
Exactly one MSI and exactly one NSIS installer, which is what `scripts/windows/artifact-inventory.mjs` fails the job over if it is not true. Uploaded as `liberty-windows-unsigned-65a47d5a481cb6fcbc599add010d9ffade70b43e` (71.2 MB, sha256:279e987d33f139b940aa89c11d6e43f90b92d1db4db20e6c2df30b5343c9c52c) and `liberty-windows-installer-logs-65a47d5a481cb6fcbc599add010d9ffade70b43e` (649 KB, sha256:b7e4553f6b3edab5c806979f8e264e6b13c992cf21e5e74489ef3027aab08d62).

THE MSI WAS ACTUALLY INSTALLED ON THE RUNNER AND ACTUALLY REMOVED, step log verbatim:
  installing apps\desktop\src-tauri\target\release\bundle\msi\Project Liberty_0.1.0_x64_en-US.msi
  installed executable: C:\Program Files\Project Liberty\liberty-desktop.exe
  packaged resource: C:\Program Files\Project Liberty\sidecar\node.exe
  packaged resource: C:\Program Files\Project Liberty\sidecar\server\server.js

So the MSI places the shell AND the packaged sidecar tree under Program Files, which is the specific thing round 95's packaging defect broke, and the uninstall leaves nothing behind.

WHAT THIS GATE DOES NOT ESTABLISH, stated because gpt-architect required it stated: "Do not call PW-0501 DONE merely because an installer is produced. A green package run proves the packaging/build gate, not installed runtime correctness." Nothing here launched the application. `liberty-desktop.exe` was never started, no window was opened, the shell never spawned the sidecar, and no handshake was exchanged on Windows. The installers are UNSIGNED and the inventory says so in its own `signingNote`; SmartScreen and Defender will trip on them. Installed runtime correctness on the commander's PC remains unevidenced and is where PW-0501's remaining work sits.

recommended.title: An LGPL-compatible libmpv and FFmpeg the product may actually ship
recommended.acceptance: The libmpv and FFmpeg binaries the installer ships are built under terms this product may distribute, and the evidence is recorded rather than assumed. docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 9 names two traps and RESEARCH_PLAYBACK.md already found the equivalent defect elsewhere -- 'every prebuilt ffprobe on npm is a GPL-3.0 binary, and several declare otherwise' -- so a downloaded build is not evidence of its own licence. REQUIRED: the configure flags that keep the build LGPL are stated and reproducible, and any GPL-only component is named and excluded. REQUIRED: the written-offer and attribution obligations LGPL imposes on a shipped binary are satisfied by something in the installer, not by a sentence in a README nobody ships. REQUIRED: the exact upstream versions are pinned and recorded, because PW-0207's error mapping is built against a specific header. NOT IN SCOPE: any decoder whose distribution needs a patent licence this project does not hold -- if one is required, stop and report it as a commander decision rather than shipping it.

recommended.title: A killed desktop dev server cannot leave a tracked file rewritten
recommended.acceptance: A desktop build or dev server cannot leave apps/web/next-env.d.ts rewritten in the working tree, under ANY termination. THE DEFECT, OBSERVED RATHER THAN PREDICTED, in round 81: the file was committed pointing at ./dist/desktop/dev/types/routes.d.ts instead of ./.next/types/routes.d.ts. Next regenerates that TRACKED file to name whichever distDir last built; the three *:desktop scripts snapshot and restore it around the child; and build-target.ts:300-342 already records that the restore happens ONLY ON NORMAL EXIT. Playwright signal-kills `next dev` when the harness finishes, so the rewrite survived, was staged by a routine `git add -A`, and was caught only by reading the diff before delivery. It typechecked locally because dist/desktop/dev happened to exist; on a fresh clone it would not have. REQUIRED: a forced termination -- SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGKILL of the child, and the parent being killed -- cannot leave the tracked file dirty. REQUIRED: THE SOLUTION MUST NOT DEPEND ON A NORMAL-EXIT CLEANUP HOOK ALONE. A second `process.on('exit')` handler is the same mechanism that already failed and would fail the same way under SIGKILL; the implementer must choose a design that is correct when no cleanup runs at all, and justify it. Two candidates, neither mandated: make the file untracked and generated (which changes what a fresh clone must do, and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md must then say so), or make the desktop distDir's type path stable so no rewrite occurs. REQUIRED: the regression is MECHANICALLY TESTED -- a test that starts a desktop invocation, kills it without letting it clean up, and fails if the tracked file differs from HEAD. A test that only exercises normal exit reproduces nothing, because normal exit already works. REQUIRED: the fix does not weaken the build-target split; build-target.test.ts must keep passing, including its assertion that no shipped module under apps/web/src names LIBERTY_BUILD_TARGET. NOT IN SCOPE: anything about product behaviour. This is a tooling defect and gpt-architect's ruling is explicit that it must not be folded into unrelated product work.
recommended.notes: Filed round 82 on gpt-architect's ruling item 4, which refused to let this stay a warning in a handoff. The scripts directory is named in allowedPaths because the three `node -e` wrappers inside apps/web/package.json are the thing that would move: JSON cannot carry a comment, which is why their reasoning currently lives in build-target.ts, and a real script file is the likeliest shape of the fix. It is not mandated -- the implementer chooses and justifies.
